name: alarm_shelve

inputBounds.hardItemsPolicyRule: a deployment may raise the 20-target default through the Runtime Target Policy and never above the 100-target hard ceiling

nativeOutcome: system.alarm.shelve reports no per-item result, so the item's own dispatch is its outcome; alarm_shelved_list state for the exact paths is the Observed state and never decides success
alarmPathForm: rendered alarm path: provider-qualified with no * (for example prov:default:/tag:Folder/Tag:/alm:AlarmName); a pattern without * matches only the source it spells out, so an exact path cannot widen to a subtree

duration.policyCapRule: a deployment may lower the maximum and never raise it

runtimeTargetPolicy.allowlistMatch: provider-qualified alarm path prefix matched at a segment boundary (/ or :); an explicit * allows every alarm path
runtimeTargetPolicy.reservedProviderRefusal: any alarm path whose prov:<provider>: component is the reserved IgnitionMCPPolicy provider, whatever the Target allowlist says, including an explicit *; a later Tag or Alarm segment that spells the name is not the provider and stays an allowlist-checked target

preflight: input, reserved provider and Target allowlist for every item before any item executes, with no rollback
deniedMutationAudit: after a usable Policy is read, a refused target produces one `decision` row and no dispatch; `off` records nothing, and `required` refuses the call when the denial row cannot be written
outcomePreservation: a dispatched batch reports its per-item outcomes whatever the Observed-state budget or the serializer does; an Observed entry that cannot be returned is an explicit `limit_exceeded` observed error, and the result is re-rendered without the Observed state rather than replacing the outcomes
itemOutcomeUnknownScope: only items whose own dispatch did not report back
